frozen_before: any V3.1 implementation, calibration, or measurement work
primary_research_question: Can Rapture remain almost invisible on normal production traffic while still obtaining exact executable incidents quickly enough when failures occur?

unchanged_from_v3: GREEDY reducer (frozen V1/V2, no algorithm change)
redaction/persist semantics for a selected request
headline bug corpus (never re-screened, never replaced)

critical_scientific_constraint.statement: A request cannot be fully captured retroactively after it has already failed.
consequences: Capture selection MUST be decided at request ingress, before the application listener is invoked.
A request not selected at ingress can never yield a full executable incident, regardless of how it ends.
The cheap detector's observation of a failure arms capture for FUTURE matching requests only.
Under targeted arming the first detected failure is normally NOT executable; the artifact comes from a later occurrence.
critical_scientific_constraint.enforcement: phase_9 no-retroactive-capture proof tests; failure there is INVALID_EXPERIMENT

hypotheses.H0: Useful exact capture requires enough always-on interception that Rapture cannot become low-overhead production infrastructure.
hypotheses.H1: A detector-only/unarmed fast path keeps steady-state successful-traffic overhead near zero while full interception activates only for selected requests.
hypotheses.H2: Ingress sampling produces a predictable overhead/capture-probability tradeoff but cannot guarantee capture of rare or one-off incidents.
hypotheses.H3: Automatic targeted arming after an initial cheaply observed failure captures a subsequent occurrence with materially better capture efficiency than random sampling for recurring incidents.
hypotheses.H4: Selective/targeted capture preserves exact failure identity, offline replay, portability, historical-fix discrimination, and current privacy gates.
hypotheses.H5: The V3 mechanism operates through at least one larger existing service application's own route and application stack without an experiment-authored replacement service route.
hypotheses.H6_NOT_TESTED: Executable incidents materially improve human or coding-agent repair (V4).
hypotheses.H7_NOT_TESTED: Teams will pay for this system.

A_ALWAYS_ON.description: Frozen V3 full capture on every request. Control/reference only.
A_ALWAYS_ON.selection_rule: every non-exempt request is selected at ingress

B_RANDOM_INGRESS_SAMPLING.description: Per-request Bernoulli selection evaluated at ingress before the application listener runs.
B_RANDOM_INGRESS_SAMPLING.rng: deterministic mulberry32 seeded by RAPTURE_V31_SEED; seed recorded per run; seeds are never replaced after observing an outcome
rules: selection is computed before the application listener is invoked
unselected requests are never retroactively upgraded, whatever their status
selected requests use frozen V3 capture semantics unchanged
observed sampled fraction is measured and reported, never assumed

C_TARGETED_ARMING.description: Cheap detector on all traffic; an observed failure automatically arms full capture for subsequent matching requests until an executable incident is obtained or the window expires.
rules: while unarmed a request runs the detector-only fast path
arming is triggered by the detector, never by the application and never by a human-supplied predicate
arming applies only to requests that arrive AFTER the arming decision
an armed matching request is selected at ingress and uses frozen V3 capture semantics
the key disarms on first persisted incident, on TTL expiry, or on request-budget exhaustion

detector_semantics.runs_on: every non-exempt request, in every strategy except A_ALWAYS_ON
allowed_observations: request pathname (url up to the first '?')
a synchronous throw escaping the application listener

normalization.rule: split pathname on '/', replace any segment matching ^[0-9]+$, a UUID, or ^[0-9a-fA-F]{16,}$ with ':id'; keep at most 12 segments; cap the result at 200 chars
normalization.caching: bounded LRU (max 512 entries) keyed by raw pathname, to keep per-request string work O(1) amortized
normalization.no_application_input: the app supplies no route table; normalization is purely lexical

detector_semantics.failure_signal: res.statusCode >= 500 OR a synchronous listener throw
forbidden_while_unarmed: recording any outbound fetch body (no Response.clone/tee)
buffering request or response body chunks
hashing any value that will be discarded

retained_state.shape: { key, armedAt, expiresAt, budgetRemaining, firstFailureAt, failuresSeen, captured }

arming_semantics.arm_condition: detector observes a failure for key K and K has no active arming
arming_semantics.select_condition: request arrives whose key K has an active arming with budgetRemaining > 0; budget is decremented at ingress
disarm_conditions: an armed request persisted an incident (SUCCESS)
arming_semantics.explicitly_reported: the failure occurrence that triggered arming is NOT executable and is reported as such in every trial record

inactive_fast_path.goal: remove V3's structural interception cost from requests not selected for high-fidelity capture
allowed_generic_work: skip AsyncLocalStorage entry entirely for unselected requests
keep pg/fetch/time/random wrappers installed globally with a minimal no-op unarmed branch
ALS quiescence: call AsyncLocalStorage.disable() when no selected request is in flight and no key is armed, so the process-wide async_hooks tax is not paid while idle
bounded LRU caches for path normalization and arming state
one 'finish' listener per request carrying only status observation
forbidden: per-framework implementation that changes semantics to rescue a benchmark
predicting failure status before request execution
buffering full DB/HTTP results in the detector-only path and calling it selective capture
inactive_fast_path.calibration_services: experiments/reproducer-v3/perf/service-a.mjs and service-b.mjs (V3 calibration services). Headline services are NOT used for optimization before implementation freeze.
inactive_fast_path.freeze_rule: the V3.1 selection/detector/capture tree is hashed and frozen after calibration and before any headline evaluation

services: V3 headline services express-qs, koa-1999, fastify-32442 at FIXED revisions (same three shapes as V3 headline perf)
performance_methodology.order: mode order randomized per repetition with a recorded seed
performance_methodology.cold_start: separated: warmup excluded from measurement; boot time recorded separately
performance_methodology.raw_data: every per-repetition file preserved; aggregation never overwrites raw

statistics.point_estimate: median across per-repetition estimates (median-of-rep-medians for latency quantiles)
statistics.interval: 95% bootstrap confidence interval over per-repetition estimates, 10000 resamples
statistics.rule: a single favorable repetition is never the reported result

capture_efficiency_metrics.sampling_reference: for rate p and n independent failure occurrences report the theoretical 1-(1-p)^n ALONGSIDE, never INSTEAD OF, empirical results

incidents.rationale: one per framework family (koa, express, fastify, hapi); each has a benign same-route request that returns 2xx on the buggy revision, so a failure RATE on one incident key is expressible without touching Rapture or application source
incidents.deterministic_only_reason: recorded before results: koa-1998 /admin and express-semver /check fail for every request on the buggy revision (no benign same-key variant exists in the frozen fixture); express-cookie and hapi-4560 are held out of the recurrence study to keep it to one incident per family

failure_profiles.name: ONE_OFF
failure_profiles.purpose: expose the fundamental limitation of post-detection arming

recurrence_workloads.trial_length: up to 20000 matching requests or until the strategy terminates (capture obtained, or arming window closed with no capture)
recurrence_workloads.rng: deterministic per-trial seed = hash(incident, profile, strategy, trialIndex); recorded; never replaced

large_application.purpose: remove the concern that V3 headline services used experiment-authored service scaffolding around real framework/repository behavior
eligibility: Node/TypeScript backend application (not a framework or library)
historical bug predating V3.1 with identifiable buggy and fixed revisions
bug observable through the application's OWN existing HTTP route
application starts through its normal application entry point
no experiment-authored replacement route implementing the bug
no application source edits to accommodate Rapture
fits the Node/http/pg/fetch boundary sufficiently for meaningful evaluation
candidate_pool: any public Node service of comparable application scale
allowed_integration: generic Rapture bootstrap (--import register.mjs) plus environment variables
a deterministic local substitute for an unavailable external service ONLY IF the application still issues its normal outbound call
headline_requirements: baseline historical bug reproduced WITHOUT Rapture first
automatic targeted capture attempted with the frozen V3.1 implementation
large_application.honesty_rule: do not weaken eligibility to force a success; if no genuinely eligible case exists after documented screening report INSUFFICIENT_LARGE_APP_CASE; if an eligible case exists and generic capture fails, that is a real negative result and is not replaced

detector_only_unarmed: 95% bootstrap upper bound for median p95 overhead <= 10% where calculable
95% bootstrap worst-side bound not worse than 10% degradation where calculable
sampling: at 1% sampling: median p95 overhead <= 5% AND median throughput degradation <= 5%
at 5% sampling: median p95 overhead <= 7.5% AND median throughput degradation <= 7.5%
10% and 25% are mapping points, not mandatory production gates
performance_hard_gates.note: thresholds are frozen here and are not adjusted after headline results are observed

correctness_hard_gates: 0 unexpected live external effects during offline replay
every targeted artifact used for headline correctness replays the exact failure 20/20
every portable headline artifact replays 20/20 from an isolated directory
the historical fixed revision removes the original failure for every evaluable targeted artifact

recurring_at_or_above_1_percent: >= 90% of trials obtain an executable incident within the bounded arming window
median additional failure occurrences after initial detection <= 1
p95 additional failure occurrences <= 2 where sample size supports estimation
targeted_capture_usefulness_gates.efficiency: fully instrumented matching requests per executable incident is reported; no post-hoc threshold is imposed on it
targeted_capture_usefulness_gates.one_off: one-off failures are expected to remain uncaptured by post-detection arming unless random sampling already selected them; this is reported as a product limitation, never as an excluded case

privacy_gates: re-run the V3 gate-tier attack suite against the final V3.1 implementation: 0 raw gate-tier leaks
detector-only mode persists no sensitive request metadata
sampled-but-successful requests leave no persisted artifact
targeted arming state contains no raw credentials, bodies, headers, or query strings
every produced executable incident is scanned
the known V3 gap tier (JWT in free text, PEM, card-like values, bare password values, base64-encoded secrets, some free-text PII) remains out-of-boundary and is NOT claimed as solved
no_retroactive_capture_proof: an unsampled one-off failure yields no full executable incident
a detector-only first failure contains no pg/fetch/time/random observations
targeted arming produces a full artifact only from a request selected at ingress
turning arming on after a response failed does not retroactively populate boundary events
manual_burden_metrics: minutes to install/configure the generic Rapture bootstrap
anti_goalpost_rules: do not claim 'always persist failures' if required pre-failure observations were not collected
do not retroactively label a detector-only failure as an executable incident
do not manually choose sampling outcomes
do not replace failed random seeds
do not tune targeted match predicates per historical bug after seeing failures
do not use known bug error codes as required predicates
do not modify capture correctness semantics merely to improve latency
do not use headline services for optimization before implementation freeze
do not remove difficult failure-rate profiles because capture probability is poor
do not hide one-off failure limitations
do not claim full production coverage from selective capture
do not proceed to agent repair simply because latency improves
do not treat theoretical sampling probability as empirical evidence

decision_rules.CONTINUE_TO_V4: detector-only/unarmed overhead is production-plausible, targeted capture obtains executable incidents efficiently for recurring failures, all exactness/privacy/portability gates hold, and selective deployment does not destroy the practical value of the primitive; large-app evidence positive or unavailable for a documented corpus reason
decision_rules.MODIFY: the mechanism remains credible but the usable deployment boundary is narrower than targeted recurring backend failures, or capture efficiency / large-app realism reveals a material limitation to resolve before repair-value testing
decision_rules.KILL: low-overhead deployment cannot be achieved without losing useful incident capture, targeted arming routinely needs many recurrences or manual predicates, exactness/privacy regresses, or an eligible large application shows the mechanism does not survive realistic application architecture
decision_rules.INVALID_EXPERIMENT: sampling enabled after outcomes are known, unsampled failures retroactively reconstructed, targeted predicates tuned per bug after results, failed trials discarded or replaced, headline implementation modified after freeze, or the large application replaced by an experiment-authored bug route
decision_rules.INSUFFICIENT_LARGE_APP_CASE: core gates pass but no genuinely eligible large-application historical case exists under the frozen boundary after documented screening
decision_rules.BLOCKED_V3_PROTOCOL: V3 cannot be honestly frozen before V3.1 begins

non_goals: no attempt to solve all V3 privacy gap classes
